entries.title: Old Mara
entries.text: An old woman who writes letters to strangers and is always right about where trouble will be. Nobody knows where she lives. Her handwriting is very old-fashioned, and so, some say, is she.

entries.title: Maraal
entries.text: Old Mara's real name. Once she rode beside the Charioteer; together they were thrown out of heaven by the Sun Spirit. She has spent a very long time choosing champions to undo what she helped begin. You are not the first.

entries.title: Reeve Halden
entries.text: The reeve of Ashford, what's left of it. He lost his village's men to the cult and refuses to lose anything else. He judges fairly and forgives slowly.

entries.title: Tomas, Halden's son
entries.text: Taken from Ashford with the other men and set to mine gold in the Sacred City's quarries. Brave, angry, and very much his father's son.

entries.title: The Smiling Peddler
entries.text: A merchant who paid double for gold and asked what a person weighs. He painted golden eyes on chapel doors so 'He' could see.

entries.title: Brother Vael
entries.text: The cult's steward in the Nether: he counts gold, skulls and people. Good at counting. Less good at being sure he's on the right side.

entries.title: The Librarian
entries.text: A scholar who has studied the cult's Old Tongue for thirty years. She can read enough of it to be properly frightened.

entries.title: Silas of the Gilded Hand
entries.text: A merchant who buys what others won't sell: skulls, blood, silence. The Gilded Hand is the cult's purse. Silas is its smile.

entries.title: The Midwife
entries.text: She ran the blood pits under the Sinful Church, where the cult tried to grow its god a new body. 'None of them ever spoke.'

entries.title: The Fixer
entries.text: The Blackwater Cartel's man in the villages: he finds growers, buyers, and people who can keep their mouths shut.

entries.title: Don Vasco
entries.text: Head of the Blackwater Cartel. Holds court in the Labyrinth. Pays a third of everything to the Chariot, and resents every coin.

entries.title: Wren the Apiarist
entries.text: A beekeeper whose bees began flying into their nests and never coming out after the light rose from the Wither's pit.

entries.title: Old Aurel
entries.text: A retired soldier of the Ashford Watch who fought piglins in his youth, and still dreams of the warrior who could not die.

entries.title: Dunn the Deserter
entries.text: A raider who threw his crossbow down at Ashford and couldn't pick it up again.

entries.title: Corwin the Refugee
entries.text: An Ashford refugee who stole grain for his sister's children.

entries.title: Wick the Informant
entries.text: A pillager scout who sold patrol times for bread. The gold, he says, goes up, never down.

entries.title: Gorran the Warden
entries.text: He locked the Bastille's doors; the cult decided who went behind them. He gave the sick his bread.

entries.title: Brann of the Garrison
entries.text: The last living soldier of the frozen garrison. His wife has thought him dead for ten years.

entries.title: Ashford
entries.text: The next village over from yours. The cult's raiders burned it and took its men, counted, not killed. What it becomes is up to you.

entries.title: The Bastille
entries.text: An illager fortress paid for in cult gold, built with cells for a hundred. Ashford's men were held there.

entries.title: The Believer's House
entries.text: A small house where a Preacher prays over the cult's prisoners on their way north.

entries.title: The Aether
entries.text: A realm above the clouds that should be full of light and is strangely empty. Something left. Or was thrown out.

entries.title: The End
entries.text: Where the second Warden waited: a dragon guarding something it had forgotten.

entries.title: The Blackwater Valley
entries.text: Where the cartel grows and sells. A third of every emerald made here goes to the Chariot.

entries.title: The Sinful Church
entries.text: A church with blood pits beneath it. The cult tried to grow its god a body here.

entries.title: The Sacred City
entries.text: The Nether Mansion: the Cult of Azazel's city of gold, its quarries worked by stolen men, its Lair at the very end.

entries.title: The Cult of Azazel
entries.text: They paint golden eyes on chapel doors. They believe gold is faith made solid, and that enough of it buys a god's favour.

entries.title: The Faithful
entries.text: The cult's warriors. They watch the roads and take people by night.

entries.title: The Divine Chariot
entries.text: The name every trail leads to. Once a charioteer of heaven; now half a god, waiting in the Sacred City.

entries.title: The Seven Wardens
entries.text: Seven great beasts that held the Chariot's pieces apart: the Wither, the Ender Dragon, and five more in the snow, the sand, the sea, the underworld and the dragon tower. Kill one, and the others grow hungry.

entries.title: The Gilded Hand
entries.text: The cult's purse: merchants who buy skulls, blood and gold, and sell anything to anyone.

entries.title: The Old Tongue
entries.text: The cult's written language. Mostly angles and anger. The Warden Journal is written in it.

entries.title: The Champions of M.
entries.text: The Dead King's crown named him 'Champion of M. Second of seven. Failed.' Maraal has done this before.

entries.title: The True Azazel
entries.text: A half-soul cannot die. To end him, his head must be joined to his body, and then he must be killed while he is whole.

entries.title: The Wither
entries.text: The first Warden, raised by the cult from three skulls in a pit you built. Where: the pit, in the overworld's open air. It died before it reached the daylight, and the Nether sky went red that night.

entries.title: The Ender Dragon
entries.text: The second Warden, guarding something in the End it had long forgotten. Where: beyond the stronghold's portal. The night it fell, every villager in the world dreamt of a king with no head.

entries.title: Skor, the Yeti
entries.text: The Warden of the snow, who kept a century-old garrison marching through the storm. Where: the Yeti Hideout, snowy plains. The day after it died, not one flake of snow fell anywhere.

entries.title: Sirok, the Sandworm
entries.text: The Warden of the sand, beneath a desert that 'breathed'. Where: the Sandworm Nest. The desert village dug its well back out, and the water came up clean.

entries.title: Nerakyss, the Kraken
entries.text: The Warden of the sea, and the black ship that sailed with it. Where: the Kraken Ship, deep ocean. The harbour lads rowed out to watch it sink. First time anyone had dared in forty years.

entries.title: Helvar, the Underworld Knight
entries.text: A knight set at the Gate by the one who took the Chariot's head. He could not speak, so he wrote it down: 'If I fall, the door will open.' Where: the Underworld Arena, in the Nether.

entries.title: Ashlord, the Infernal Dragon
entries.text: The last Warden, and once the Chariot's own mount. Where: the Dragon Tower. The smith said nothing alive was as hard as its bones.

entries.title: The Old Tongue
entries.text:
The cult calls him Azazel. The Aether's hymn calls him Azriel. Neither is his name. His name was a word in the Old Tongue, something like 'the one who carries the sun across', and every time a mouth says it, a little of him comes back.
That is why the Faithful pray in angles and never in names. They are not afraid of offending him. They are afraid of feeding him.
You know the word now. You won't write it here.

entries.title: The Last Pilgrim
entries.text:
Oren has walked the roads for fifty years. He taught village children their letters and their numbers, and one of them was a quick, quiet boy called Vael, who loved to count.
The cult found Vael at fifteen and taught him what to count: gold, skulls, people. Oren has been looking for him ever since, not to bring him home, only to tell him the count is done.

entries.title: What the God Saw
entries.text:
He wasn't thrown out of the sky. She was. The Sun Spirit cast Maraal down for loving the one who carried the sun, and he let go of the reins and jumped after her.
He caught her. The fall split him in two when they landed: the half that caught her, and the half that hated the sky for letting her go. The cult worships the second half. Maraal has spent every year since trying to find the first.

entries.title: Sky and Fire
entries.text:
The piglins remember a war nobody else does: the sky against the fire, fought by two halves of the same god. The gold half kept the sky. The iron half kept everything else.
Gilded blackstone is where the sun bled when the halves tore at each other. The cult mines it and calls it holy. The piglins mine it and call it a scar.

entries.title: Clean Hands
entries.text:
Silas doesn't believe in clean hands. In his trade, everybody's are dirty: the trick is only knowing whose.
So he sent a thief to find your secret, and the thief found nothing, and that frightened Silas more than any blade. A person with nothing to hide is a person who cannot be bought.
